correctness.rationale: For a part-preserving H, the orbit-barycenter model exactly parametrizes fixed geometric points. The closed-neighborhood criterion is equivalent to at least one part having occupancy at most one; in the fixed complex that is exactly the stated cover. All proper nonempty cover intersections have a full simplex on orbits of an omitted part and are contractible, while the total intersection is the join of discrete globally fixed vertex sets. Cofibration Mayer–Vietoris/nerve calculations yield the stated suspension count or the boundary-of-simplex case, including zero-fixed-vertex and singleton-fixed-vertex boundaries. A 233-case independent graph-adjacency and mod-two homology checker corroborates, but does not replace, the general integral homotopy proof.

value.rationale: Ambient wedge types and permutation modules cannot describe geometric fixed point sets. The theorem provides a natural full classification for arbitrary part-preserving subgroups of a familiar highly symmetric graph family, and detects contractibility and sphere dimensions ranging from the number of parts minus two up to twice that number minus two depending on fixed vertices. The exact transition through zero, one, or at least two fixed vertices in a part is a structural isotropy invariant that may be used in equivariant topology and graph Čech models; it is neither a parameter increment nor an arbitrary finite slice.
